Subject: Post-call: PraxisBio dedicated capacity, isolation needs & SLA projection

Hi Ava / Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap while it's still fresh and to confirm next steps. I've grouped notes into pain/goals, technical fit & constraints, and proposed next actions so we can align internal owners.

Pain & goals (as stated on the call)
- Model footprint: ~2B param family for inference, median sequence length ~512 tokens, peaks to ~2048 for some batches.
- Latency requirement: p95 <= 180ms for single-request interactive use; background batch scoring can tolerate higher latencies.
- Data isolation: PHI-sensitive workloads; PraxisBio requires tenant isolation and evidence of KMS integration.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly throughput target to keep cost within procurement budget.

Qualification notes / constraints
- Target start: Q3 pilot (Aug) with ~2 GPUs reserved initially, scaling to 8 reserved within 3 months if benchmarks meet expectations.
- Preferred region: us-west (data residency and latency).
- Compliance: require SOC 2 Type II report copy and audit log retention for 12 months.

Proposed SLA/ops targets (ballpark)
- Uptime: 99.9% monthly for dedicated pool
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms on pinned model variant under continuous batching policy
- Support: 24x5 with 1-hour P1 response during business hours for pilot

Attachments I shared: PraxisBio_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (high-level throughput math), Draft_SLA_PraxisBio_v1.pdf (starter language)

Next actions & owners
1) Rishi: run an internal fit-check with the serving team on the model profile (memory footprint + quantization feasibility) — ETA Tue 5/19
2) Ben: provide a short ops-runbook sketch for tenant isolation & KMS integration and confirm burst policy options — ETA Fri 5/22
3) Jasmine (me): follow up with procurement to get their standard PO timeline and share the initial SLA draft — I will send the doc by EOD tomorrow
4) Ava / Samir: confirm the pilot target dataset size (approx tokens per day) and whether audits require an on-prem option — please reply with the data point or a calendar slot for a quick follow-up.

If that aligns, I'll open a tentative HubSpot deal stage (qualification) and schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi and your infra lead next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Subject: RE: Post-call: PraxisBio dedicated capacity, isolation needs & SLA projection

Thanks for the notes, Jasmine — did a quick back-of-envelope on the config. Initial thoughts: 

- Model sizing: for a ~2B param family at fp16/AMP-equivalent, we estimate ~40-48 GB GPU memory with KV cache headroom for 2k seq lengths. Best to target 80GB-class GPUs for the pilot unless Praxis will accept quantized int8 variants.
- Throughput: with continuous batching tuned for median seq=512, a 2x GPU cluster (2x80GB) should handle ~60-80 reqs/sec with p95 latency near target in typical traffic distribution. Scaling to 8 GPUs looks reasonable to keep p95 headroom as traffic increases.
- Isolation: Tenant isolation via dedicated pool + VPC peering + per-tenant KMS keys is achievable. Ops change: we recommend a separate subnet per tenant and mandatory audit-log forwarding to Praxis's logging endpoint (or we can host logs with role-limited access).

Open technical questions for Praxis (to confirm during the deep-dive):
1) Are you okay with an 80GB GPU baseline for the pilot or do you require strict <=48GB instance types?
2) Any regulatory constraints on where audit logs are stored (can't leave US-west)?
3) Expected concurrency distribution (spiky vs steady).

I'll put together a short one-pager (config options: 80GB baseline, int8 variant tradeoffs, burst policy examples) and share it with the thread by 5/19 so Ben and I can align on the ops runbook.

-r
